settings.label: Project URL
settings.meaning: The project's API address. Auth, Edge Functions and Storage are paths under it.
settings.whereToFind: The dashboard's Connect dialog: https://<project-ref>.supabase.co. Supabase has no test mode: test is another project, or a Branching branch, each with its own URL and keys.

settings.label: Publishable key
settings.meaning: Names the project on calls made for a signed-in user, alongside the user's own token. Safe in a browser: what it may do is what Row Level Security allows.
settings.whereToFind: Settings › API Keys: the publishable key (sb_publishable_…), or the legacy anon key while it still works.

settings.label: Secret key
settings.meaning: Calls Auth's admin API and Edge Functions as the app. It bypasses Row Level Security, so it never leaves the server; Supabase refuses it from a browser.
settings.whereToFind: Settings › API Keys › Secret keys: a secret key (sb_secret_…), or the legacy service_role key while it still works. Supabase deprecates the legacy keys by the end of 2026.

settings.label: Auth Hook secret
settings.meaning: Checks that an HTTP Auth Hook's request came from Supabase Auth.
settings.whereToFind: Authentication › Hooks, on the HTTP hook: its secret, v1,whsec_<base64>. Join two with | while rotating.

settings.label: S3 access key id
settings.meaning: With its secret, reads and writes the project's buckets through Storage's S3 endpoint, for @mariachi/storage.
settings.whereToFind: The project's Storage settings (dashboard/project/<project-ref>/storage/settings): S3 access keys, a new access key. The S3 connection must be enabled there too.

settings.label: S3 secret access key
settings.meaning: The access key's secret. It reaches every bucket and bypasses Row Level Security, so it never leaves the server.
settings.whereToFind: Shown with the access key id when the key is made.

settings.label: S3 region
settings.meaning: The region Storage's S3 endpoint signs requests for: the project's region.
settings.whereToFind: The project's Storage S3 page (dashboard/project/<project-ref>/storage/s3): the region shown with the endpoint.

operations.name: functions.invoke
operations.purpose: Calls an Edge Function by name with a JSON body: as the app (the secret key), or for a signed-in user (their token, with the publishable key).

operations.name: admin.users.list
operations.purpose: Lists the project's users, a page at a time.

operations.name: admin.users.create
operations.purpose: Creates a user with an email address (and optionally a password), confirmed or not. Sends no email.

operations.name: admin.users.invite
operations.purpose: Invites a user by email: Supabase Auth sends the invitation, whose link signs them in.

operations.name: admin.users.delete
operations.purpose: Deletes a user, or soft-deletes them.

signature.description: Standard Webhooks: webhook-id, webhook-timestamp (Unix seconds) and webhook-signature, a space-separated list of v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256 of "<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<raw body>">, keyed with the base64-decoded part of the secret after v1,whsec_. Each hook is configured with its own URL, so the route names the hook.

events.meaning: Supabase Auth wants an email sent (sign-up, invite, magic link, recovery, email change, reauthentication, or a notification), with the token to put in it.
Supabase Auth wants an SMS sent with a six-digit one-time code.
A user is about to be created; the answer may reject it.
An access token is about to be issued; the answer gives its claims.
A user tried to verify an MFA factor; the answer may reject it.
A user tried to sign in with a password; the answer may reject it.
